The integrated scope, schedule and cost baselines, used to manage, measure and control execution.
The authorized budget assigned to the scheduled work; excludes management reserve.
The budget for the work actually performed, measured without reference to actual cost.
The cost actually incurred for the work performed in the same period.
The sum of all budgets for the work: the project cost baseline.
CV = EV − AC; SV = EV − PV. Negative: over budget, behind schedule.
CPI = EV / AC; SPI = EV / PV. Below 1.0: over budget, behind schedule.
EAC = BAC / CPI.

front: EAC when the rest goes as planned
back: EAC = AC + (BAC − EV): the variance was a one-off.

front: EAC when the plan is no longer valid
back: EAC = AC + bottom-up ETC.

front: EAC when CPI and SPI both matter
back: EAC = AC + [(BAC − EV) / (CPI × SPI)].
ETC = EAC − AC (or a reestimate). VAC = BAC − EAC; negative means over budget at the end.
(BAC − EV) / (BAC − AC), or with EAC. Work remaining over funds remaining; above 1.0 is harder.
0/100: no credit until done, for work within one period. 50/50: half at start, for two or three periods.
Weighted, verifiable milestones for longer work; percent complete needs measurable criteria.
Support work (quality assurance, inspection, testing) valued as a percentage of related discrete work.
Non-measurable work; EV always equals PV, so it never shows a schedule variance.
EVM measures, the WBS and control thresholds let managers act only where needed; thresholds set formal reporting.

Updating the PMB after approved changes; changes only future work, hides no past issues, formally approved.
Replanning: realign the remaining work to meet the original target. Reprogramming: a new over-target baseline or schedule.
Work performance data (raw) → information (compared with the plan) → reports (for decisions).
PV and EV in story points times a rate per point; EV only for accepted stories (0 or 100%); AC from recorded hours.
